rules.title: Block search indexing with noindex
rules.summary: A noindex rule in a meta tag or HTTP header tells Google to drop the page from search results. Pages that must rank must not carry noindex.
rules.whyGoogleCares: Google will not rank a page it has been told to exclude from the index.
rules.fixHint: Remove the noindex meta tag / X-Robots-Tag header and request reindexing.

rules.title: Introduction to robots.txt
rules.summary: robots.txt controls which URLs crawlers may fetch. A Disallow on a URL prevents Googlebot (and, via their own tokens, AI crawlers) from reading it.
rules.whyGoogleCares: If Google cannot fetch the URL it cannot evaluate or rank its content.
rules.fixHint: Remove the Disallow for the affected path, and verify no CDN/WAF rule blocks the bot's user agent or IP ranges.

rules.title: Control snippets in search results
rules.summary: nosnippet, data-nosnippet and max-snippet limit how much text Google may show. AI features that quote source text are suppressed where snippets are disallowed.
rules.whyGoogleCares: AI Overviews and AI Mode build answers from snippet-eligible content; blocking snippets removes the page as a usable source.
rules.fixHint: Remove nosnippet / data-nosnippet from content you want cited, or set a generous max-snippet.

rules.title: Understanding Core Web Vitals and Google Search results
rules.summary: Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) measure loading, interactivity and visual stability. 'Good' thresholds are LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1.
rules.whyGoogleCares: Page experience is a ranking signal; a slow or unstable template can lose to faster competitors on close calls.
rules.fixHint: Optimise the slowest template: image sizing, render-blocking resources, main-thread work and layout reservations.

rules.title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
rules.summary: Content should satisfy the searcher's intent. If no page directly answers a query, there is nothing for Google or AI engines to surface.
rules.whyGoogleCares: Search and AI answers reward pages that comprehensively and clearly answer the question being asked.
rules.fixHint: Create or expand a page that directly and thoroughly answers the prompt, with clear headings and supporting entities.

rules.title: Search Essentials
rules.summary: When competitors are consistently cited, their pages better demonstrate relevance, experience and authority for the query.
rules.whyGoogleCares: AI answers and organic results cite the sources that best demonstrate E-E-A-T for the query.
rules.fixHint: Study the cited competitor pages; close gaps in depth, freshness, structured data and demonstrated expertise.

rules.title: Scaled content abuse
rules.summary: Generating many pages primarily for ranking, with little value to users, is a spam policy violation regardless of how they are produced.
rules.whyGoogleCares: Scaled low-value content degrades search quality and is subject to manual and algorithmic action.
rules.fixHint: Do not mass-produce near-duplicate pages; create fewer, genuinely useful pages.

rules.title: Doorway abuse
rules.summary: Sites or pages created to rank for similar queries (e.g. many near-identical city pages) that funnel users to one destination are doorways.
rules.whyGoogleCares: Doorway pages exist to manipulate rankings rather than serve users.
rules.fixHint: Consolidate near-duplicate location pages into genuinely distinct, useful pages.

rules.title: Site reputation abuse
rules.summary: Publishing third-party content on a host site mainly to exploit the host's ranking signals is site reputation abuse.
rules.whyGoogleCares: It launders the host domain's authority onto content the host does not stand behind.
rules.fixHint: Do not host third-party pages to borrow a domain's authority; keep content first-party and editorially owned.
